- Relevant past episodes/treatments: No similar prior episodes; no previous surgeries; no prior hospital care for this issue.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported or noted.
- Airway/breathing: Patient denies dyspnea or cough; no stridor reported.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; reports mild nausea.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: Not applicable (telehealth encounter).

Assessment:
- Abdominal pain with possible urinary tract infection; no ENT involvement identified.  
  Justification: Gradual lower abdominal pain, pink urine, increased frequency, mild systemic symptoms; no airway or ENT symptoms.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:  
  • Empiric antibiotic treatment—Trimethoprim one tablet twice daily for 3 days.  
  • Analgesia—Paracetamol as needed.  
  • Hydration encouraged; cranberry juice suggested.
- Specific instructions:  
  • Perform a home pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy.  
  • Monitor symptoms and temperature.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:  
  • Worsening abdominal pain, persistent or high fever, onset of vomiting, urinary burning, or any new respiratory/ENT symptoms (e.g., throat tightness, voice change, breathing difficulty).  
  • Seek urgent care or call emergency services if red flags develop.
- Follow-up: Return or contact clinic in a few days if no improvement or if symptoms worsen; further investigations (urinalysis, abdominal assessment) to be arranged if necessary.  
  • No ENT or allergy referral required at this stage.

● Missing/expected data: Drug/food allergy list; documented vitals; physical abdominal and ENT examination findings; prior anaphylaxis management plan (not relevant here but routinely expected in ENT/allergy consults); availability of auto-injector not applicable.
